title: Disease Burden and Clinical Characteristics of Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis at the Thoraxklinik and Heidelberg University Hospital: A Mixed-Methods Study
summary:
Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) is a long-term fungal lung disease that mainly affects people with pre-existing lung conditions. Diagnosis and long-term treatment are often difficult because its symptoms can overlap with those of other lung diseases.
In this study, existing medical records from the Thoraxklinik Heidelberg and the Department of Infectious Diseases and Tropical Medicine at Heidelberg University Hospital will be reviewed to better understand how people with CPA are diagnosed, treated, and cared for.
In addition, interviews will be conducted with affected patients to explore their personal experiences with the disease, its treatment, and everyday life.
By combining both approaches, the study aims to improve our understanding of medical care as well as the challenges and needs of people living with CPA.

interventions.name:
The study has two methodologically distinct components:

Substudy 1: Retrospective analysis of existing routine clinical data from patients with confirmed chronic pulmonary aspergillosis who underwent diagnostic evaluation or received treatment at Heidelberg University Hospital or the Thoraxklinik

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Teilstudie 1– Retrospective cohort:
- Confirmed chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) based on available medical records.
- Documented diagnostic evaluation or treatment at Heidelberg University Hospital or the Thoraxklinik Heidelberg between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025.

Teilstudie 2 – Qualitative interviews:
- Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) documented by a medical specialist.
- Capacity to provide informed consent.
- Written informed consent for study participation and audio recording.
- Sufficient German language proficiency to participate in a semi-structured interview.
Exclusion criteria:
Teilstudie 1 – Retrospective cohort:
- Isolated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA).
- Aspergillus spp. colonization without chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.
- Invasive aspergillosis without preceding chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.
- Subacute invasive aspergillosis present at the index date.

Teilstudie 2 – Qualitative interviews:
- Inability to provide informed consent.
- No specialist-documented diagnosis of chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.
- Insufficient German language proficiency.
- No consent for audio recording.
